title: Package-qualified pin table
description: library/parts/<MPN>/pins.yaml. The authoritative pin table transcribed from the manufacturer's pin list, qualified by package. A different package variant is a different table until proven identical -- QFN and LQFP versions of one die routinely number differently, and assuming otherwise silently poisons every pin check downstream.

package.description: Must match a package entry in part.yaml.

identical_to_package.description: Set only when the manufacturer explicitly states pin numbering is identical to another package, with a citation proving it. Never inferred.

source.description: Where this pin table was transcribed from, including the page and table so a reviewer can re-check it in one step.

number.description: Pad/pin number exactly as the manufacturer prints it. Always a string: BGA numbering is alphanumeric (A1, B12) and exposed pads are often numbered oddly, so numeric typing would corrupt them.

name.description: Primary pin name from the manufacturer pin list.

type.description: Electrical character of the pin, used for logic-level and driver-conflict checks.

aliases.description: Other names the manufacturer uses for the same pin.

boot_strap.description: True if this pin's level at reset selects a boot or configuration mode. Drives the boot/strap conflict check.

must_connect.description: Manufacturer requires this pin to be connected (e.g. a second VDD, or an exposed pad that is the only ground return). Absence of a connection is then an error, not a warning.

no_connect_reusable.description: Whether an NC pad may be repurposed. Defaults false: NC pads are frequently internally bonded, and assuming otherwise is a classic dead-board cause.
